issue_fixed: The settlement engine accepted external proofs only from an intent's maker or taker, so the governance-managed Settlement gateway could verify and finalize external state but could not submit the proof that advances the intent.
implementation: Add SettlementProofOrigin to the settlement-engine Config.
Wire the runtime to the existing storage-backed EnsureSettlementGateway origin.
Accept an intent party or the authorized proof origin for submit_proof, submit_cross_domain_proof_set, and submit_btc_proof.
Keep claim_settlement and refund_settlement restricted to the intent parties.
Charge one additional database read for proof-origin authorization.

verification.command: SKIP_WASM_BUILD=1 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo clippy -p pallet-x3-settlement-engine -p x3-chain-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings

negative_and_boundary_tests: An ordinary signed third party cannot submit an EVM proof.
An ordinary signed third party cannot submit a BTC proof.
The authorized settlement relayer can submit an EVM proof and cross-domain proof set.
The authorized settlement relayer cannot claim an intent leg.
The authorized settlement relayer cannot refund an intent.
An authorized relayer reaches BTC proof verification and is refused for the unanchored header, rather than being refused for origin.
limitations: This establishes the chain-side authority and custody boundary. The relayer executable still does not bind a runtime intent id into queued evidence or submit the typed runtime extrinsic.
No live Sepolia, Solana devnet, or Bitcoin testnet transaction was submitted.
The governance-managed Settlement gateway remains a chain-configured trust boundary and has not yet completed external audit.
